author: rdc-rfc1-author-a (Claude Haiku 5.5)
rationale: The release chain and q run on gclk, the output of the black-box clock gate cg_cell. The clock's identity and edges cannot be established, so the synchroniser and its release cannot be checked.

author_reading.rationale: The release chain is clocked by a gated clock from a cell not in the design, so whether its clock is synchronous to the source clock cannot be decided.

labels.rationale: The synchroniser and the data register are clocked by gclk from an opaque clock-gating cell. The clock is unidentified, so the chain cannot be recognised and its clock edge and synchroniser quality are undecided.
labels.detection_gap: The gated clock comes from an opaque cell, so RDC-003 and CST-004 can only report it as unresolved.

labels.rationale: The two stages and receiver share the gated clock. The missing gate implementation leaves pulse shape and restart behavior undecided, including whether enough valid clock edges arrive to release reset.
labels.suspected_flaw: The cell is defined as an empty module without a black-box attribute. Its output is undriven in the literal RTL.

settlement.rationale: Both readers are right on unknown. A's class is kept. The settler added (* black_box *) to cg_cell on line 3, fixing B's undriven-module flaw. CST-005 reports the black box, and RDC-003 (b) and CST-001 report the reset registers with no identified clock. CST-004 (A) concerns the d capture, not the reset. CDC-002 and CST-011 (B) are outside the reset question.
